title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Builds a systems-level understanding of environmental science while developing the data literacy, ethical reasoning, and policy awareness needed to analyze real environmental problems and possible solutions.

topics.title: Environmental Science as an Interdisciplinary Field
topics.description: This opening topic defines environmental science as a bridge among natural systems, human systems, data, ethics, and decision-making.

children.title: Environmental literacy
children.description: Students learn the basic vocabulary and habits needed to interpret environmental problems.

children.title: Interdisciplinary problem framing
children.description: Environmental questions cross science, economics, policy, culture, and justice.

children.title: Data and scientific reasoning
children.description: Students practice reading environmental evidence rather than treating claims as slogans.

topics.title: Earth Systems and Planetary Boundaries
topics.description: Environmental science starts with Earth as an interacting system of air, water, land, life, and human activity.

children.title: Earth system spheres
children.description: Students learn how the atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere, biosphere, and anthroposphere interact.

children.title: Feedbacks and thresholds
children.description: Feedbacks explain why environmental change can accelerate, stabilize, or cross tipping points.

children.title: Planetary boundaries
children.description: This gives a global frame for evaluating human pressure on Earth systems.

topics.title: Energy Flow and Biogeochemical Cycles
topics.description: Matter cycles and energy flows are the backbone of ecosystems and environmental change.

children.title: Energy flow
children.description: Students learn how energy enters, moves through, and leaves ecological systems.

children.title: Major cycles
children.description: Biogeochemical cycles connect organisms, soils, oceans, air, and rocks.

children.title: Human alteration of cycles
children.description: Students connect agriculture, fossil fuels, and land use to disrupted cycles.

topics.title: Population Growth, Consumption, and Resource Use
topics.description: Environmental impact depends on population, consumption, technology, and institutions, not population alone.

children.title: Population dynamics
children.description: Students learn the demographic patterns behind growth and stabilization.

children.title: Consumption and ecological footprints
children.description: Resource use varies widely across places and societies.

children.title: Resource limits and substitution
children.description: Students examine scarcity, efficiency, and tradeoffs.

topics.title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
topics.description: Biodiversity supports ecosystem function, resilience, culture, food, medicine, and economies.

children.title: Biodiversity patterns
children.description: Students learn biodiversity at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels.

children.title: Ecosystem services
children.description: Students connect ecological processes to human well-being.

children.title: Biodiversity threats
children.description: Students identify major drivers of biodiversity loss.

topics.title: Water, Air, and Soil Systems
topics.description: Water, air, and soil are the life-support media where many environmental problems become visible and measurable.

children.title: Water systems
children.description: Students learn how water moves through watersheds, aquifers, and human infrastructure.

children.title: Air systems
children.description: Atmospheric processes control weather, climate, pollution transport, and human exposure.

children.title: Soil systems
children.description: Soils connect geology, ecology, agriculture, water, and carbon storage.

topics.title: Climate Change Science
topics.description: Climate change is a central case for understanding evidence, mechanisms, impacts, mitigation, and adaptation.

children.title: Climate system basics
children.description: Students learn how greenhouse gases, radiation, and feedbacks shape climate.

children.title: Evidence and impacts
children.description: Students connect observed data to physical and ecological consequences.

children.title: Mitigation and adaptation
children.description: Students distinguish reducing causes from managing unavoidable impacts.

topics.title: Energy Systems and Decarbonization
topics.description: Energy choices shape climate, air quality, land use, water use, economics, and justice.

children.title: Energy sources
children.description: Students compare fossil, nuclear, and renewable energy systems.

children.title: Energy transitions
children.description: Transitions involve technology, infrastructure, policy, and behavior.

children.title: Energy justice
children.description: Students examine who bears harms and who receives benefits.

topics.title: Pollution Sources, Pathways, and Fate
topics.description: Pollution becomes an environmental problem through sources, transport pathways, exposure, persistence, and transformation.

children.title: Pollution types
children.description: Students learn major pollutants and their environmental behavior.

children.title: Transport and fate
children.description: Pathways explain where pollutants go and who is exposed.

children.title: Monitoring and prevention
children.description: Students connect pollution science to control strategies.

topics.title: Environmental Health, Risk, and Toxicology
topics.description: Environmental health links exposures in air, water, food, soil, and workplaces to human and ecosystem outcomes.

children.title: Exposure and dose
children.description: Students learn that risk depends on contact, concentration, duration, and vulnerability.

children.title: Risk assessment
children.description: Risk frameworks help compare hazards and make decisions under uncertainty.

children.title: Precaution and communication
children.description: Students practice explaining risk responsibly.

topics.title: Food, Agriculture, and Land Use
topics.description: Food systems connect soil, water, biodiversity, climate, labor, technology, and culture.

children.title: Agricultural systems
children.description: Students compare industrial, agroecological, and smallholder systems.

children.title: Land-use change
children.description: Land conversion drives habitat loss, emissions, and hydrologic change.

children.title: Sustainable food systems
children.description: Students evaluate pathways for feeding people while reducing harm.

topics.title: Oceans, Coasts, and Freshwater Resources
topics.description: Aquatic systems concentrate many environmental challenges: water supply, fisheries, pollution, climate impacts, and coastal risk.

children.title: Freshwater resources
children.description: Students learn water scarcity, allocation, and watershed management.

children.title: Ocean systems
children.description: Oceans regulate climate and support major food webs.

children.title: Coastal change
children.description: Coasts reveal interactions among sea level, storms, ecosystems, and infrastructure.

topics.title: Sustainability, Environmental Justice, and Ethics
topics.description: Environmental decisions involve fairness, power, responsibility, and different visions of a good future.

children.title: Sustainability frameworks
children.description: Students learn common ways to evaluate long-term human-environment well-being.

children.title: Environmental justice
children.description: Students examine unequal exposure, participation, and benefits.

children.title: Environmental ethics
children.description: Ethical frameworks clarify how people value species, ecosystems, and future generations.

topics.title: Environmental Policy, Governance, and Economics
topics.description: Science matters most when it can inform institutions, incentives, rules, and collective action.

children.title: Policy tools
children.description: Students learn the tools governments and communities use to reduce environmental harm.

children.title: Governance scales
children.description: Environmental governance happens locally, nationally, and globally.

children.title: Environmental economics
children.description: Economic concepts help explain market failures and policy design.

topics.title: Environmental Data, GIS, and Remote Sensing
topics.description: An introductory course should introduce students to how environmental patterns are measured, mapped, and monitored.

children.title: Environmental indicators
children.description: Students learn to interpret the numbers used in public environmental debates.

children.title: GIS and Mapping
children.description: Maps reveal spatial patterns in hazards, resources, exposure, and land change.

children.title: Remote sensing
children.description: Satellite data help monitor forests, fires, water, cities, and climate impacts.

topics.title: Field, Lab, and Case-Study Methods
topics.description: Students need practice turning environmental questions into evidence, analysis, and decisions.

children.title: Sampling design
children.description: Good environmental data starts with clear questions and defensible sampling.

children.title: Quality assurance and uncertainty
children.description: Students learn that methods and uncertainty shape conclusions.

children.title: Case-study synthesis
children.description: Complex problems require integrating science, stakeholders, and tradeoffs.
